scope: Browser test fixtures only; no production lifecycle or project-close behavior changed.

recentProjects.observedFailure: On Windows, deleting the complete project directory immediately after closeProject returned EPERM; deleting only .novalist passed.
evidence: The failed project directory had normal Directory attributes and was removable after its test process exited.

An isolated diagnostic retried the exact deletion while Electron stayed open: attempts 0 through 5 returned EPERM, then attempt 6 succeeded after approximately 600 ms. All original recent-project assertions passed.
On the installed Node v26.7.0, synchronous rmSync still failed in three repetitions with maxRetries: 5 and retryDelay: 100. Awaited node:fs/promises rm with the same options passed.
recentProjects.limitation: These checks demonstrate a transient directory lock but do not identify its native owner or establish when it first appeared.
recentProjects.change: Await native asynchronous rm with recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 5, retryDelay: 100 for the complete project directory. Keep the existing assertions and close each test app in finally.
recentProjects.retryBound: At most five native retries, with the configured linear delay of 100 ms per retry; no assertion retries or swallowed deletion failures.

electronTeardown.observedFailure: The detached-window test completed its assertions, then hung during ElectronApplication.close. A runtime image/audio protocol test had also intermittently hung during teardown.
evidence: A fresh Chromium profile did not prevent the detached-window teardown hang.
Removing window-all-closed listeners alone did not prevent the hang. After the timeout, the test Electron main process remained while its backend and renderers had exited.
The installed Playwright close implementation evaluates app.quit through the Node inspector before closing that inspector connection and awaiting the application-close event.
Deferring the bound real app.quit with setImmediate allowed the inspector evaluation to return before Electron shutdown. Both pane-window cases then passed across three repetitions.
electronTeardown.diagnosis: The teardown evidence supports an inspector/shutdown ordering race. Electron can wait for the attached inspector during shutdown while Playwright is still waiting for its app.quit evaluation to finish.
electronTeardown.change: The test fixture removes window-all-closed listeners before destroying its temporary windows and defers the bound real app.quit with setImmediate. Playwright initiates the quit after the fixture destroys the windows.
electronTeardown.preserved: The real bound quit method, before-quit, will-quit, and backend disposal remain active. Production shutdown code is unchanged.
